name: Propranolol
lead: Propranolol is a non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker developed by Scottish pharmacologist James Black in the 1960s, patented in 1962 and first marketed as Inderal in 1965.[1][2] It is prescribed for hypertension, angina, arrhythmias, migraine prevention, essential tremor and infantile hemangioma.[1][2][3]

It is also used off-label for situational and performance anxiety, where it reduces physical symptoms such as tremor and racing heartbeat.[1][2] A 2025 meta-analysis reported no benefit over placebo or benzodiazepines for social phobia or panic disorder, though evidence quality was limited.[2]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed for social anxiety and, in some threads, for claimed bone or growth effects, which the cited preclinical research does not establish in humans. It is prescription-only in the US, UK, EU and Australia.[2][4]

paras: The US label lists hypertension and other cardiovascular and neurological indications.[4] Propranolol was the first beta blocker effective for coronary artery disease and hypertension; Black shared the 1988 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for beta-blocker work.[2] A 2008 NEJM report described its effect on severe infantile hemangiomas.[3]

Propranolol is occasionally used for performance anxiety by blocking adrenaline's physical effects.[1][2] It has been used in precision sports such as shooting and archery; a 2008 Olympic shooter was stripped of medals after a positive test.[2]

It competitively blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors, reducing heart rate, contractility and blood pressure.[1] Research on emotional memory shows beta-adrenergic activation enhances memory for emotional events, motivating studies in post-traumatic stress.[2][5]

Common effects include fatigue, bradycardia, nausea and abdominal pain. It can worsen asthma and is contraindicated in severe bradycardia, heart block, decompensated heart failure and cardiogenic shock. The label warns of exacerbated angina and, in some cases, myocardial infarction after abrupt discontinuation.[1][2][4]

On looksmax.org, users discuss propranolol for physical symptoms of social anxiety, with some reporting it helps with physical anxiety but not anxiety in general, and others warning of side effects.[6][7] One thread argues it could stimulate bone growth, citing laboratory findings on IGF-1 and BMP-2 in bone cells; the thread itself notes that most of this evidence is preclinical in rodents.[6] Other threads ask where to obtain it without a prescription; this article does not describe sourcing.

Controlled evidence exists for cardiovascular indications, including post-infarction beta-blockade, and for infantile hemangioma.[3][8] For anxiety, the 2025 meta-analysis noted above found no benefit over placebo in social phobia and panic disorder.[2] Registered trials examine propranolol in dental anxiety, post-traumatic stress and other conditions.[9][10] No clinical studies of propranolol for bone growth or appearance were found.

lore.intro: Forum discussion centers on propranolol for social anxiety and, in some threads, claims about bone growth, with side effects and access also discussed.[6][7]

claims.claim: Propranolol calms the physical symptoms of social anxiety.
claims.believers: Users report it helps with physical anxiety such as shaking and heart racing.[6]
claims.experts: The drug is used off-label for performance anxiety to block physical symptoms, though a 2025 meta-analysis found no benefit over placebo for social phobia or panic disorder.[2]

claims.claim: Propranolol stimulates bone growth via IGF-1 and BMP-2.
claims.believers: One thread cites cell and rodent studies reporting raised local IGF-1 and BMP-2 expression in bone-forming cells.[6]
claims.experts: No clinical studies of propranolol for bone growth or height in humans were found; the thread itself describes most evidence as preclinical.[6]

claims.believers: Users warn of side effects, including sexual side effects.[7]
claims.experts: The label lists bradycardia, heart failure and other cardiovascular effects and warns against abrupt discontinuation.[4]

card.summary: Prescription beta blocker used off-label for performance anxiety; the forum bone-growth theory is untested in humans.
card.note: Abrupt discontinuation can worsen angina; contraindicated in asthma and heart block.

quick.overview:
Propranolol is a long-established prescription beta blocker for blood pressure, heart rhythm, migraine prevention and tremor. It is also used off-label to ease the physical symptoms of performance anxiety.

Forum users discuss it for social anxiety and, in some threads, bone growth; the bone claim comes from cell and animal data and has not been studied in people.
quick.mechanism: It blocks beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors, blunting the effects of adrenaline on heart rate and tremor.
quick.risks: Common effects include fatigue, slow heart rate and nausea; it can worsen asthma, and abrupt stopping is warned against. It is prescription-only in most countries.
